name: toc-rail
title: Contents rail
description: A quiet contents rail for long articles: one mark per heading in the page gutter, opening into the titles on hover, focus or a touch button.
docs: Put it in a column of the page next to the article, in the outer gutter, and leave about 16rem free there: the rail is 2.5rem wide at rest and grows over the gutter, never over the text. Pass items (id, title, level 1 to 3) in page order; the ids are the ids of the headings. It follows the scroll by itself, or takes activeId. offset is the room, in px, a fixed header takes: the rail sticks that far from the top and a heading counts as reached when it passes that line (give the headings scroll-margin-top to match). side="left" mirrors it. It is a nav with a list of links and aria-current="location": a mouse opens it by pointing, the keyboard by Tab, and a small button, drawn only where the pointer is a finger, holds it open (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange). Below the lg breakpoint it is hidden: put a contents control at the top of the article for phones.
